personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: A ledger I can read, with every try written down, helps me keep the teams on one way of running jobs.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: Writing our own queue sounds like more fluff unless a jam is impossible to miss.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: I want my laws working across repositories, though this first step only brings back the knowledge part.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: I don't master the harness, so I only care that it works without me touching it.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: It stays out of my code, and fewer silent failures means less slop reaching production.

objection.text: I already see this tool as a gimmick, and now you're writing your own queue. When it jams at 3am, how would I even know?

rounds.fit: Fits the lead engineer best and the skeptical back-end developer worst, until a jam opened an issue by itself.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: Five tries, a claim that runs out and a replay give me what I need when a job fails.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: An issue opening by itself answers my worry, and two tables is less fluff than I feared.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: My specs get judged again, but the outbox check staying off still holds some of my repositories back.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: Nothing changes on my screen, and my PRDs get judged again, which is what I need.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: It never touches the front end, so I have no reason to object.

rounds.fit: Fits the lead engineer best; the outbox check staying off is what the product manager feels most.
